comment: Advisories the audit gate may see at high or critical severity without failing.
An entry is a dated statement that the flaw is not reachable in THIS tree, with the
measurement that establishes it. It is not a judgement that the advisory is wrong.
`scripts/audit-gate.sh` refuses an advisory that is not here, an entry whose `until`
has passed, and an entry that no longer matches anything — a dead exemption is as much
a defect as a missing one, because it is a claim nobody has to justify any more.
Adding an entry therefore costs a dated reason that survives two readers.

why: The flaw is in RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature VERIFICATION accepting extra nested
DigestAlgorithm elements. No version fixes it: node-forge 1.4.0 is the latest the
registry holds, the advisory's range is `*`, and npm reports `fixAvailable: false`.
`acme-client@5.4.0` is likewise the latest and still asks for `node-forge: ^1.3.1`,
so an `overrides` pin cannot help the way it did for axios.
Measured unreachable in three links on 2026-10-05.
(1) `node_modules/acme-client/src/crypto/forge.js` is labelled by its own author as a
`Legacy node-forge crypto interface`, nothing inside acme-client imports it — the
single reference is a re-export at `src/index.js:34` — and what it exposes is key
generation, CSR reading and CSR SIGNING. The word `verify` does not appear in it.
(2) `@ipshipyard/libp2p-auto-tls` is the only consumer of acme-client here, and it does
not touch `acme.forge`: it handles keys through WebCrypto
(`dist/src/utils.js:94-95`, `crypto.subtle.importKey`). Its own `forgeEndpoint` and
`forgeDomain` name the libp2p.direct registration service — a collision of the word
`forge`, not a use of node-forge.
(3) No production source in this repository imports acme-client. `local-acme.ts` is this
project's ACME SERVER for a loopback authority, so acme-client is the thing under
test there rather than something this code calls.
And it is absent from what is deployed: `packages/cloudflare/package.json` depends on
neither auto-tls nor acme-client, so the hosted node does not carry node-forge at all.
The single path is `@o2/node -> @ipshipyard/libp2p-auto-tls -> acme-client -> node-forge`,
which a self-hosted backbone node would run.
Removing the dependency was weighed and refused for now: `NET-03`'s AutoTLS half rests
on it, along with seven measured cases in `auto-tls.node.test.ts` and `local-acme.ts`.
Owner ruling 2026-10-05, taken with that cost named.
